A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, Structured Preconditioners in Adaptive Optimization: A Unified Analysis. All 40 pages, including Appendices A–E, support comparison of the text, equations, tables and figures without material evidence gaps.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic linear-regression optimization experiments in Section 5, EMA comparisons and learning-rate sweeps in Appendix E, and a numerical counterexample in Appendix A.4.2.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental and numerical results, including Figures 1–3 and the computed matrices in Appendix A.4.2.

M1.justification: The AdaReg, EMA and Shampoo preconditioning procedures are retained. Algorithms 4–5 change iterate-index conventions, and Section 3.3.1 expands block notation, without introducing a different preconditioner, objective or substantive update mechanism.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same synthetic matrix linear-regression problem. The new discussion of language-modeling experiments in Section 6 attributes those experiments to concurrent work by An et al.; it does not expand this paper's evaluated tasks.

E2.justification: Figure 1 retains AdaGrad-Norm, diagonal AdaGrad and full-matrix AdaGrad as comparators to one-sided Shampoo. Figure 2 retains AdaSGD, Adam and full-matrix AdaSGD. ASGO and DASGO are discussed only as related work, not added experimental baselines.

E3.justification: Section 5 and Appendix E retain the same initialization, 100 optimization steps, last-iterate and average-iterate loss metrics, 60 learning rates from 1e-4 to 1e2, and EMA settings. The theorem-level learning-rate corrections do not document changed experimental protocols.

E4.justification: The learning-rate sensitivity analysis in Figure 3, EMA comparisons in Appendix E.2 and numerical counterexample in Appendix A.4.2 are unchanged. Remark 2.3 adds interpretation of an existing counterexample rather than a new analysis or robustness test.

E5.justification: Both versions report learning-rate tuning and averaging across five seeds. Neither adds repeated runs, confidence intervals, significance tests or a different uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Figures 1–3 contain identical plotted results, and Appendix A.4.2 retains the same numerical matrices. The reported experimental findings remain unchanged, including one-sided Shampoo performing best and full-matrix AdaGrad worst in Figure 1.

T1.justification: Theorems 3.8 and 3.14 add explicit learning-rate conditions. Theorem 4.4 changes the learning-rate multiplier from sqrt(2) to sqrt(2/d_R), and Theorem 4.5 restores a missing factor of two in its optimized regret bound. Appendix C also revises existing proof steps, including the EMA inequality chain. These are localized corrections within the retained theoretical framework.

C1.justification: The abstract, main contributions and conclusion retain the same claims: a unified analysis of structured preconditioners, improved bounds for one-sided Shampoo, and evidence that greater adaptivity need not improve optimization.

C2.justification: New Remark 2.3 explains that Example 2.2 concerns exact minimization over a poorly structured cone. Actual two-sided Shampoo uses a fixed, nondecreasing preconditioner and avoids that issue. This substantively clarifies the counterexample's applicability without changing it.

D1.justification: v2 makes the learning-rate requirements accompanying the convergence guarantees explicit and corrects the documented scaling for one-sided Shampoo in Theorem 4.4. This refines algorithm-parameter guidance; the experimental implementation, precision, epsilon, EMA coefficients and memory-efficient implementation in Appendix E.1 remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 6 adds An et al. (2025), identifying ASGO with one-sided Shampoo and describing DASGO as a blockwise Adam instance covered by the framework. The corresponding reference is added; the broader research positioning is retained.

P1.justification: Localized edits add Remark 2.3, clarify blockwise notation in Section 3.3.1, adjust pseudocode indexing and expand explanations in Appendix C. The section organization and most prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Appendix C promotes dense expressions to numbered displays, and localized reflow changes theorem placement and moves Figure 2 lower on its page. Algorithm input lines are compacted. Tables 1–2 and the contents, axes and legends of Figures 1–3 are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 improves precision through explicit learning-rate conditions and corrected factors in Theorems 4.4–4.5. Remark 2.3 prevents a misleading interpretation of the Shampoo counterexample, while clearer proof presentation and acknowledgment of concurrent ASGO work improve readability and positioning. These are useful, localized gains; the core framework and empirical support remain unchanged.
